en.headline: Three arrested over Mong Kok One Piece card shop scam involving HK$1.47 m
en.dek: Police say 44 victims paid for game cards at a Nathan Road shop that suddenly closed; two local men and a foreign woman were detained on Tuesday on suspicion of obtaining property by deception.
body: Police arrested three people on Tuesday in connection with a suspected scam at a game-card shop on Nathan Road in Mong Kok. Officers said they had received multiple reports since 15 August from customers who ordered and paid for goods either in person or online, after which the shop closed and its social-media accounts were deactivated.

A total of 44 victims have been identified, with individual losses ranging from about HK$900 to HK$42,000 and a combined total of approximately HK$1.47 million. The shop mainly sold One Piece trading cards. Game cards believed to be related to the case were seized from the home of one of the suspects.

The three detainees — two local men aged 42 to 50 and a foreign woman — are being held for investigation on suspicion of obtaining property by deception. The case is being handled by the Mong Kok District Crime Investigation Team 8. Police appealed to anyone who had dealings with the shop and suspects they may have been defrauded to report the matter.

zh.headline: 旺角海賊王卡牌店涉走數 44人損失147萬元拘三人
zh.dek: 警方指受害人向彌敦道一間遊戲卡店訂貨付款後店舖突結業，兩名本地男子及一名外籍女子周二被捕，涉嫌以欺騙手段取得財產。
body: 警方周二拘捕三人，涉嫌與旺角彌敦道608號一間遊戲卡店的懷疑騙案有關。警方自8月15日起接獲多人報案，指受害人透過實體或網上途徑向該店訂購貨物並付款後，店舖突然結業，相關社交媒體帳號亦告關閉。
警方初步調查相信涉及44名受害人，損失金額介乎約900元至4.2萬元，總額約147萬元。該店主要售賣日本漫畫《海賊王》遊戲卡。人員其後在其中一名被捕男子住所檢獲一些遊戲卡片，相信與案件有關。
三名被捕人包括兩名42至50歲本地男子及一名外籍女子，現正被扣留調查，案件列作以欺騙手段取得財產，交由旺角警區刑事調查隊第八隊跟進。警方呼籲曾光顧該店或懷疑受騙的市民報案。
